components.name: LED — Light Emitting Diode
components.why: An LED converts electrical current into light. Unlike a light bulb, it only allows current to flow in ONE direction — from anode (+) to cathode (−). It emits almost no heat and lasts thousands of hours.
components.polarityNote: The LONGER leg is the anode (+). Connect it toward power. The SHORTER leg is the cathode (−). Connect it toward GND. Reversed = no light.

components.name: Resistor — 220Ω
components.why: A resistor limits current flow. Without it, an LED connected to 5V would draw far more than its 20mA maximum and burn out instantly.
components.polarityNote: Resistors have no polarity — either direction works.

components.name: Potentiometer — 10kΩ
components.why: A potentiometer is a variable resistor. Turning the knob moves a wiper across a resistive track, producing a voltage between 0V and VCC on the middle pin — perfect for analog input.
components.polarityNote: Outer pins go to 5V and GND (either order); the middle pin (wiper) is the signal.
